subject: Post-call: evaluation alignment & parity acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@novafin.com>, Daniel Park <dpark@novafin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: evaluation alignment & parity acceptance criteria

Thanks again for carving out time earlier, Sarah + Daniel — good discussion. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we have a single source of truth coming out of the discovery: 

What we heard (from NovaFin)
- Primary goal: Replace the existing in-house paraphrase/ranking stack ("Acme Paraphrase 2.1") for customer-facing summarization & query rewriting while keeping or improving accuracy.
- Constraints: 100 ms median token latency budget per request (applies to streaming), hard SLA for P95 latency at peak; tight data residency in us-east for production.
- Acceptance: Need clear parity thresholds vs the proprietary baseline (metrics and sample prompts) before moving to a pilot.

Redwood proposed evaluation scope (what we'll run first)
1) Metric suite: Exact-match/normalized-EM (for extraction tasks), ROUGE-L and BLEU for summarization, and a factuality-focused precision-at-1 on a curated failure-set (we'll share methodology).
2) Models to trial (initial): open variants (Llama-3-70B-4bit, Mistral-Base-16k quantized) vs our Redwood-Prod-Base-v1 (32-bit float) as the production baseline.
3) Prompt & dataset: We'll use the prompt set you supplied (attached: novafin_promptset_v2.jsonl) and augment with the 120-case regression set you mentioned.
4) Acceptance criteria (proposal): 
   - For primary tasks, open model must be within ±3% absolute on the chosen quality metric vs Acme Paraphrase 2.1 AND not exceed a 20% uplift in user-visible error modes (hallucinations, missing entities) on the curated failure-set.
   - Latency: median per-request token latency must be <= 100 ms for the targeted instance size, and P95 <= 250 ms during synthetic peak load.

Immediate next steps (actionable & owners)
- Redwood (Monica/Tessa): run two parallel eval passes (open models vs Redwood-Prod baseline) on the prompt set + failure-set. Deliver a CSV with metric breakdowns and flagged examples by Tue EOD (May 11).
- NovaFin (Sarah/Daniel): confirm which 120-case regression set to prioritize (if different from the attached) and confirm whether PII redaction is required for any examples.
- Redwood (Rishi): prepare an acceptance checklist and a short UX risk memo that calls out likely regression classes and mitigation strategies (fallback routing to a higher-tier model).

Attachments: novafin_promptset_v2.jsonl, open_vs_prop_eval_results_20270509.csv (provisional schema)

If you're good with the acceptance bullets above I'll lock them into the evaluation ticket and kick off runs.

Thanks — Rishi

From: Sarah Ellis <sarah.ellis@novafin.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 14:02:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: evaluation alignment & parity acceptance criteria

Thanks Rishi — that recap is super helpful. A couple of clarifications before you run the evals: 

1) Acceptance bounds: the ±3% on the primary metric makes sense, but for factuality we prefer an absolute floor (not relative). Can we require open models to achieve >= 92% precision-at-1 on the failure-set? If they don't, we'd want a mitigation plan (e.g., reroute to the proprietary model for those intents).

2) Latency: the 100 ms median is for in-region (us-east) optimized instances. If the open model needs different instance sizing (e.g., 70B model on 1xA100 vs 2xA100), that's fine — as long as the cost/throughput tradeoff is documented.

3) Prompts: we'll review novafin_promptset_v2.jsonl and flag PII. If any redaction is required we'll push that back to you by Mon noon.

Please include HubSpot deal link in your ticket so our procurement team can start the SOW discussions early.

—Sarah

Head of ML Product, NovaFin
sarah.ellis@novafin.com

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Sarah. Confirming the updated acceptance criteria per your note: 
- Primary metric parity: open model within ±3% absolute of Acme Paraphrase 2.1 on task-level metrics.
- Factuality: open model must hit >= 92% precision-at-1 on the curated failure-set or we'll tag those intents for fallback routing.
- Latency: median <= 100 ms in us-east for the selected instance; P95 <= 250 ms at synthetic peak.
